nominees.name: Toy Battle
nominees.description: Command an army of toys in tactical skirmishes where childhood nostalgia meets strategic warfare.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic tactical movement with dice combat and simple unit abilities. T(2): Toy theme is cute but doesn't generate childhood wonder mechanically. G(2): Standard tactical decisions with limited strategic depth or consequence. F(2): Miniature setup and rules reference create moderate overhead. Ar(3): Colorful toy aesthetic appeals but lacks atmospheric depth.

nominees.name: Civolution
nominees.description: Guide a civilization through millennia of development, making crucial decisions that shape humanity's destiny across multiple eras.
nominees.justification: M(4): Tech trees, multi-use cards, and era progression create deep interconnected systems. T(3): Civilization development theme present but mechanics feel more abstract than generative. G(4): Every tech choice and card play shapes your civilization's trajectory meaningfully. F(2): Solo setup and rules complexity manageable but era transitions add overhead. Ar(4): Clean historical artwork with appealing visual progression through technological ages.

nominees.name: L'île des Mookies
nominees.description: Explore a mystical island, collecting magical resources and building structures to become the most powerful island inhabitant.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic action points and tile placement without complex interactions. T(2): Island exploration theme sits on top of abstract mechanics. G(2): Meaningful choices but limited decision trees and consequences. F(2): Standard setup time with moderate component management overhead. Ar(3): Colorful tropical art style that's pleasant but not exceptional.

nominees.name: Zenith
nominees.description: Navigate a modular space station collecting energy crystals while managing limited actions and competing for optimal paths.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic action point allocation with simple movement and collection. T(2): Space theme applied as window dressing on abstract mechanics. G(2): Limited meaningful choices constrained by action economy. F(3): Modular setup and component management create overhead. Ar(2): Functional but uninspiring sci-fi artwork lacks atmospheric depth.

nominees.name: Odin
nominees.description: Lead Viking clans across treacherous seas and foreign lands, building settlements and claiming glory in Odin's name.
nominees.justification: M(4): Complex worker placement with asymmetric clan powers and interlocking systems. T(3): Viking theme present but mechanics don't generate epic saga experience. G(4): Deep decision trees with meaningful long-term consequences across multiple boards. F(2): Heavy setup and rules overhead typical of Uwe Rosenberg designs. Ar(4): Atmospheric Norse art with quality components and board design.

nominees.name: Kutna Hora
nominees.description: Transform a medieval mining town into a silver empire through guild politics, cathedral construction, and cutthroat economics.
nominees.justification: M(4): Asymmetric guilds, worker types, tech tracks create interlocking engine systems. T(2): Medieval silver mining theme sits on top of Euro mechanics. G(4): Deep decision trees with guild powers and multi-use cards. F(2): Setup complexity and multiple boards add overhead but manageable. Ar(4): Rich medieval artwork and detailed component design throughout.

nominees.name: Operation Noisette
nominees.description: A French children's card game about collecting nuts where squirrels gather acorns through simple matching.
nominees.justification: M(1): Basic card matching with minimal interaction or depth. T(1): Nut collection theme purely decorative, not mechanically integrated. G(1): Random draws limit meaningful decision-making opportunities. F(5): Foreign language rules, unclear availability, children's game barriers. Ar(1): Presumed simple children's illustration style without atmospheric depth.

nominees.name: Behind
nominees.description: Navigate shadowy corridors while something unknown stalks you from behind in this minimalist horror chase.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic movement and pursuit mechanics without deep interaction systems. T(2): Horror theme exists but mechanics don't generate genuine dread or tension. G(2): Limited meaningful choices in straightforward chase scenarios. F(3): Obscure 2003 game likely has clunky rules and components. Ar(2): Early 2000s production values with minimal atmospheric visual design.

nominees.name: Trio
nominees.description: Collect sets of three matching cards in this simple trick-taking variant that rewards pattern recognition.
nominees.justification: M(1): Draw cards and match sets with minimal decision depth. T(1): No thematic content, pure abstract card matching. G(1): Limited hand size constrains meaningful choices significantly. F(1): Instant setup with basic card game rules. Ar(2): Standard playing cards offer functional but uninspiring visual design.

nominees.name: La Famiglia: The Great Mafia War
nominees.description: Rise through the ranks of warring Sicilian crime families in 1980s Palermo, where every deal could be your last.
nominees.justification: M(3): Action points with area control and family management systems. T(4): Every extortion, hit, and territory grab IS the mafia power struggle. G(3): Meaningful choices in violence versus politics but constrained options. F(2): Rules overhead and multiple boards create setup friction. Ar(4): Atmospheric crime family artwork captures 1980s Sicily tension perfectly.

nominees.name: Mon Puzzle Aventure - Dragon
nominees.description: Draw paths and solve spatial puzzles while following a dragon's journey through illustrated fantasy landscapes.
nominees.justification: M(1): Basic path-drawing puzzles with minimal interconnected systems. T(1): Dragon is cosmetic decoration over generic puzzle mechanics. G(2): Puzzle solutions offer some meaningful path-finding choices. F(1): Pick up book and start drawing immediately. Ar(2): Generic fantasy illustration without distinctive visual identity.

nominees.name: Faraway
nominees.description: Draft sanctuary cards in reverse order to guide a lost traveler through an alien world back to civilization.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple drafting with reverse-order scoring creates light puzzle. T(3): Journey theme emerges through backwards narrative revelation. G(3): Draft choices matter for scoring combos and story flow. F(1): Minimal components, instant setup, clear rules. Ar(4): Evocative alien landscapes with clean, atmospheric illustrations.

nominees.name: Akropolis
nominees.description: Build an ancient Greek city by drafting hexagonal tiles and stacking them into a three-dimensional metropolis, scoring points for districts and quarries.
nominees.justification: M(3): Tile drafting with 3D stacking creates spatial puzzles and set collection. T(2): Ancient Greek theme is pleasant decoration without mechanical generation. G(3): Meaningful choices in tile selection and placement optimization each turn. F(1): Quick setup, clear rules, smooth gameplay flow. Ar(4): Beautiful ancient Greek aesthetic with clean geometric tile design.

nominees.name: Ark Nova
nominees.description: Build the world's greatest zoo by drafting cards, managing conservation projects, and racing toward fame on parallel scoring tracks.
nominees.justification: M(4): Card drafting with action selection, upgrade paths, and interlocking zoo systems. T(2): Zoo theme is pleasant but mechanics don't generate conservation experience. G(4): Meaningful card drafts and action choices with long-term consequences. F(2): Setup time and icon learning create moderate overhead. Ar(4): Clean, professional zoo art with strong visual hierarchy.

nominees.name: Flashback: Zombie Kidz
nominees.description: Kids travel back in time to prevent a zombie apocalypse by solving memory puzzles and making story choices.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple memory and deduction mechanics with light narrative branching. T(3): Time travel premise creates some thematic tension in choices. G(2): Limited agency through memory challenges and story decisions. F(1): Quick setup, simple rules designed for accessibility. Ar(3): Kid-friendly cartoon zombie art, functional but not atmospheric.

nominees.name: Challengers!
nominees.description: Draft fighters into your deck and battle through tournament rounds where only the strongest decks survive elimination.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple deck building with creature powers but limited interaction depth. T(2): Fighting tournament references theme but doesn't generate tension or drama. G(2): Draft choices matter but gameplay feels automated once decks clash. F(2): Multiple phases and tournament structure create moderate setup overhead. Ar(3): Clean cartoon fighter art serves function without inspiring atmosphere.

nominees.name: 7 Wonders: Architects
nominees.description: Draft cards to build your ancient wonder faster than your rivals in this streamlined civilization race.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple card drafting with basic resource matching and wonder building. T(1): Ancient civilization theme is pure decoration over abstract mechanics. G(2): Card choices matter but limited options and streamlined play. F(1): Family-weight game with quick setup and simple rules. Ar(3): Clean but unremarkable art, functional wonder boards lack atmosphere.

nominees.name: Dune: Imperium
nominees.description: Navigate the deadly politics of Arrakis through spice, schemes, and strategic alliances in the battle for the Imperium's throne.
nominees.justification: M(4): Deck building with worker placement creates rich synergies and strategic depth. T(3): Political maneuvering feels Dune-like but mechanics reference more than generate. G(4): Every card play and agent placement cascades into meaningful consequences. F(2): Setup and multiple boards create overhead but manageable complexity. Ar(4): Stunning desert palette and iconic Dune imagery throughout.

nominees.name: Bubble Stories
nominees.description: Navigate branching underwater adventures through a storytelling card system where your choices shape the ocean's mysteries.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple card-driven branching narrative with minimal mechanical depth. T(3): Ocean exploration emerges through narrative choices and discovery. G(2): Meaningful story branches but limited mechanical agency. F(2): Card management and story tracking create some overhead. Ar(3): Functional underwater aesthetic without standout visual appeal.

nominees.name: Living Forest
nominees.description: As a nature spirit, simultaneously reveal symbol cards to collect trees and animals while managing the sacred fire that sustains the forest.
nominees.justification: M(3): Simultaneous card reveal with push-your-luck symbols and tile collection. T(2): Forest spirit theme applied over abstract symbol matching mechanics. G(3): Meaningful risk assessment on every card reveal and collection choice. F(2): Multiple decks and tiles create setup overhead and rules complexity. Ar(4): Lush forest artwork with appealing nature spirit aesthetic by Apolline Etienne.

nominees.name: MicroMacro: Crime City
nominees.description: Detectives examine a massive illustrated cityscape to solve interconnected crimes by following visual clues across time and space.
nominees.justification: M(2): Hidden object search with case connections but minimal mechanical depth. T(1): Crime theme is purely decorative overlay on visual puzzle mechanics. G(2): Some meaningful deduction choices but mostly linear clue following. F(1): Unfold map and start playing immediately. Ar(4): Detailed Wimmelbild illustration style with charming visual storytelling.

nominees.name: The Crew
nominees.description: A space crew must complete increasingly complex missions using only cryptic hints and silent teamwork in this cooperative trick-taking adventure.
nominees.justification: M(2): Trick-taking with mission constraints but limited mechanical depth. T(2): Space theme is decorative, doesn't generate crew experience. G(3): Meaningful card play decisions within communication restrictions. F(1): Quick setup, elegant rules, immediate play. Ar(3): Clean functional design but lacks atmospheric immersion.

nominees.name: Dragomino
nominees.description: Explore a magical island as young dragons, collecting domino tiles to build landscapes and discover baby dragons in their eggs.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple domino placement with basic pattern matching requirements. T(2): Dragon theme is charming but mechanics don't generate fantasy. G(2): Limited meaningful choices in tile selection and placement. F(1): Family game with immediate setup and simple rules. Ar(4): Cute dragon art appeals to families, pleasant visual design.

nominees.name: Oriflamme
nominees.description: Noble houses deploy knights with hidden agendas in a medieval court where timing your reveals determines victory or death.
nominees.justification: M(2): Hidden role cards with simple timing decisions, minimal interaction depth. T(2): Medieval theme sits on mechanics rather than emerging from them. G(3): Meaningful timing choices on when to reveal cards matter significantly. F(1): Quick setup, simple rules, plays in twenty minutes smoothly. Ar(3): Functional medieval art without atmospheric depth or distinctive style.

nominees.name: Res Arcana
nominees.description: Harness mystical artifacts and essences to fuel ancient monuments and transcend to arcane mastery.
nominees.justification: M(4): Deep artifact combinations with essences creating intricate engine optimization puzzles. T(2): Mystical theme overlays mechanics but doesn't generate magical experience. G(4): Every artifact purchase and essence management decision cascades meaningfully. F(2): Setup and iconography learning curve moderate but manageable. Ar(4): Elegant mystical artwork with rich colors and atmospheric symbols.

nominees.name: The Mind
nominees.description: Play numbered cards in ascending order without speaking, relying only on shared intuition and perfect timing.
nominees.justification: M(1): Play cards in numerical order - minimal mechanical complexity. T(1): Abstract numbers with no thematic layer whatsoever. G(1): Success depends on luck and timing, not meaningful decisions. F(1): Shuffle cards and play immediately. Ar(2): Plain numbered cards with basic geometric design.

nominees.name: Detective
nominees.description: Detective investigators use real-world databases and websites to solve interconnected murder cases that blur the line between game and reality.
nominees.justification: M(4): Complex deduction web connecting multiple cases with real internet research. T(5): You ARE investigating — using actual police databases creates authentic detective work. G(4): Every lead followed and connection made shapes case resolution meaningfully. F(2): Setup and website navigation add friction to gameplay flow. Ar(4): Gritty crime scene photography and evidence cards enhance investigative atmosphere.

nominees.name: Mr. Wolf
nominees.description: Detective work meets fairy tale noir as you investigate Mr. Wolfe's alleged crimes through deductive case files.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic deduction with card reveals and clue matching. T(3): Fairy tale detective theme carried through narrative but not deeply embedded. G(3): Deductive choices matter but limited agency in linear cases. F(2): File-based format requires some organization and reference checking. Ar(3): Functional noir-fairy tale aesthetic without exceptional visual design.

nominees.name: Azul
nominees.description: Draft colorful tiles from a Moorish palace's marketplace to create stunning azulejo patterns on your royal wall.
nominees.justification: M(2): Pattern matching and set completion with light spatial puzzles. T(1): Tile decoration theme is pleasant but purely cosmetic. G(3): Meaningful drafting choices and tile placement optimization each turn. F(1): Simple rules, fast setup, elegant component handling. Ar(4): Beautiful tile art evoking Portuguese azulejo craftsmanship.

nominees.name: Terraforming Mars
nominees.description: Transform the red planet into a living world by drafting corporations, playing cards, and raising temperature while competing for terraforming glory.
nominees.justification: M(4): Deep engine building with interlocking card synergies and resource systems. T(2): Mars theme overlays optimization puzzle but doesn't generate planetary transformation fantasy. G(4): Every card draft and placement shapes long-term engine efficiency. F(2): Setup and iconography learning curve with lengthy play sessions. Ar(4): Clean board design with effective Mars imagery and card art.

nominees.name: Nom d'un renard !
nominees.description: Young detectives race against time to gather clues and catch the fox who stole Mrs. Plumpert's prized pot pie.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple roll-and-move with basic deduction and clue gathering. T(3): Detective work feels authentic through evidence collection mechanics. G(2): Cooperative decisions but limited by dice rolls and simple choices. F(1): Family game with quick setup and intuitive rules. Ar(3): Charming children's book illustration style, well-executed but simple.

nominees.name: Unlock!
nominees.description: Build decks of Care Bear magic to spread friendship and unlock the power of caring across Cloud Kingdom.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic deckbuilding with friendship tokens and simple card interactions. T(1): Care Bears theme is pure decoration over standard mechanics. G(2): Deck choices matter but limited by child-friendly design constraints. F(1): Simple rules and setup for family accessibility. Ar(2): Bright colorful art but saccharine aesthetic clashes with user preferences.

nominees.name: Scythe
nominees.description: Command diesel-punk mechs across Eastern Europa, harvesting resources and conquering territories in an alternate 1920s where the Great War never ended.
nominees.justification: M(4): Asymmetric faction powers with interlocking resource economy and mech upgrades. T(2): Beautiful art but mechanics feel like Euro with mech decoration. G(4): Multiple victory paths with meaningful timing and positioning decisions. F(4): Large box with many unpainted miniatures requiring assembly or painting. Ar(5): Jakub Rozalski's haunting 1920+ artwork is absolutely stunning and iconic.

nominees.name: Kikou le Coucou
nominees.description: Stack wooden eggs in a wobbly nest while a cuckoo clock bird threatens to knock everything down.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple stacking with minor dexterity challenge, limited systems interaction. T(2): Nest-building theme present but mechanics don't generate bird experience. G(2): Some risk assessment in placement but mostly luck-driven outcomes. F(1): Wooden components, instant setup, teach in minutes. Ar(3): Charming wooden aesthetic but lacks visual impact or atmosphere.

nominees.name: Mysterium
nominees.description: A murdered ghost communicates only through abstract visions, guiding psychic investigators to solve his own death before time runs out.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple card drafting and clue matching with limited depth. T(4): Abstract art cards generate genuine psychic communication experience perfectly. G(2): Ghost player has choices but investigators mostly guess randomly. F(2): Setup involves sorting many vision cards by difficulty. Ar(4): Ethereal, atmospheric artwork creates haunting séance mood beautifully.

nominees.name: Maître Renard
nominees.description: One player becomes the cunning fox while others hunt as forest animals in this asymmetric deduction game.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple asymmetric roles with basic card play and deduction. T(2): Fox-and-hunters theme sits on top of mechanics. G(2): Limited meaningful choices, mostly card selection and bluffing. F(1): Light rules, quick setup, family-friendly complexity. Ar(3): Functional woodland art, nothing special but adequate.

nominees.name: Colt Express
nominees.description: Program your moves in advance then watch chaos unfold as bandits rob a speeding train in the Wild West.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple programmed movement with basic action selection across train cars. T(2): Wild West theme overlays mechanics but doesn't generate tension. G(2): Programming creates some meaningful choices but limited decision space. F(2): 3D train setup and programmed action phases add overhead. Ar(3): Colorful cartoon Western style functional but not atmospheric.

nominees.name: Five Tribes: The Djinns of Naqala
nominees.description: Manipulate ancient tribes across desert sultanates, invoking djinn magic to claim territories and treasures in mystical Naqala.
nominees.justification: M(4): Mancala movement creates chain reactions with djinn powers and bidding systems. T(2): Arabian theme decorates mechanics without generating mystical experience. G(4): Every meeple pickup creates cascading decisions across multiple scoring paths. F(2): Rules complexity and AP-prone turns slow gameplay flow. Ar(4): Gorgeous Clément Masson illustrations capture Arabian Nights atmosphere beautifully.

nominees.name: La Chasse aux Gigamons
nominees.description: Command giant monsters in tactical combat, rolling dice to power devastating attacks across destructible cityscapes.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic action points with dice rolling for combat resolution. T(1): Kaiju theme is cosmetic overlay on generic tactical combat. G(2): Movement and attack choices matter but limited tactical depth. F(2): Standard setup with multiple dice types and terrain tracking. Ar(2): Functional monster art but lacks atmospheric polish or distinctive style.

nominees.name: Loony Quest
nominees.description: Draw lines on transparent sheets to guide your character through obstacle-filled levels in this dexterity-puzzle adventure.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple draw-on-transparency mechanics with basic scoring puzzles. T(1): Video game theme is pure decoration over dexterity mechanics. G(2): Route planning choices but limited decision depth per level. F(1): Quick setup, simple rules, immediate play. Ar(3): Colorful cartoon aesthetic that's pleasant but not striking.

nominees.name: Concept
nominees.description: Use only symbols and icons to help your team guess words and phrases without speaking a single word.
nominees.justification: M(1): Point at icons on a board — minimal mechanical depth. T(1): Communication theme referenced but not generated by mechanics. G(2): Some creativity in icon selection but limited meaningful choices. F(1): Open box and start pointing immediately. Ar(3): Clean iconography serves function but lacks atmospheric appeal.

nominees.name: Bruxelles 1893
nominees.description: Commission art nouveau masterpieces in Belle Époque Brussels while building your cultural empire through cunning auction bids and gallery placements.
nominees.justification: M(4): Worker placement with auctions, multi-use cards, and interlocking art commissions. T(2): Art nouveau theme is pleasant but mechanics don't generate artistic experience. G(4): Every auction bid and worker placement carries significant strategic weight. F(3): Complex setup with multiple boards and card management overhead. Ar(4): Beautiful period-appropriate art nouveau styling throughout all components.

nominees.name: Riff Raff
nominees.description: Balance wooden pieces on a swaying pirate ship while the seas rock beneath you, hoping your cargo doesn't tumble into the depths.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple stacking with physics but limited strategic depth. T(1): Pirate theme is decorative overlay on abstract balancing. G(2): Some skill in placement but physics dominates outcomes. F(2): Setup and explanation easy but dexterity requirement excludes some. Ar(3): Charming wooden ship design but simple component aesthetic.

nominees.name: Les Bâtisseurs - Moyen-Âge
nominees.description: Draft workers and buildings to construct medieval monuments faster than your rivals in this lightweight engine builder.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple worker-building matching with basic resource conversion chains. T(1): Medieval theme is pure decoration over abstract optimization mechanics. G(2): Draft choices matter but optimal paths become obvious quickly. F(1): Small box, simple rules, fast setup and play. Ar(2): Generic medieval art lacks personality or atmospheric depth.

nominees.name: Andor
nominees.description: Young heroes venture through the magical kingdom of Andor, solving quests and protecting the realm from emerging threats.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple action points and movement on fixed board with basic quest mechanics. T(3): Fantasy adventure actions align with heroic theme but don't generate tension. G(2): Limited meaningful choices constrained by simplified children's game design. F(1): Streamlined rules and setup designed for young players. Ar(4): Charming fantasy illustrations in established Andor visual style.

nominees.name: Myrmes
nominees.description: Build an underground ant colony by managing specialized castes, expanding tunnels, and nurturing larvae through seasonal cycles.
nominees.justification: M(4): Complex worker placement with caste specialization and multi-layered colony management. T(2): Ant theme is present but mechanics feel generic worker placement. G(4): Meaningful decisions about caste development and tunnel expansion strategies. F(2): Setup overhead and multiple boards create some complexity barriers. Ar(4): Clean, functional art with appealing ant colony aesthetic throughout.

nominees.name: Tino Topini
nominees.description: Outsmart your opponents as clever mice collecting cheese while avoiding the dangers of a shifting household.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic card play with simple set collection mechanics. T(2): Mouse theme is decorative overlay on standard card mechanics. G(2): Limited meaningful choices constrained by random card draws. F(2): Simple setup but rules clarity issues from obscure German release. Ar(2): Functional cartoon mouse art without distinctive visual appeal.

nominees.name: X-Wing Miniatures Game
nominees.description: Pilot iconic starfighters in tactical dogfights where pre-programmed maneuvers and precise positioning determine who lives and dies in the vacuum of space.
nominees.justification: M(4): Programmed movement with pilot abilities and upgrade combinations create tactical depth. T(4): Movement dials and positioning generate genuine starfighter combat tension. G(4): Every dial selection and target choice carries life-or-death consequences. F(3): Pre-painted miniatures but requires movement templates and dial management. Ar(4): Stunning pre-painted starfighters with excellent Star Wars aesthetic.

nominees.name: Takenoko
nominees.description: Tend a magical bamboo garden where a hungry panda disrupts your carefully planned cultivation.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple action selection with basic tile placement and set collection. T(2): Cute panda theme overlaid on abstract optimization mechanics. G(2): Straightforward decisions with limited interaction and consequences. F(1): Family-weight game with clean setup and intuitive rules. Ar(4): Charming kawaii art style with excellent panda miniature.

nominees.name: Olympos
nominees.description: Guide ancient civilizations through history by balancing technological advancement with divine knowledge on parallel development tracks.
nominees.justification: M(3): Dual track system with tech trees and divine knowledge creates interesting choices. T(2): Civilization theme present but mechanics feel abstract rather than thematic. G(3): Meaningful decisions on resource allocation and timing advancement. F(2): Setup and tracking dual progress systems adds moderate overhead. Ar(3): Clean functional design but lacks atmospheric punch for ancient civilizations.

nominees.name: Sherlock Holmes détective conseil
nominees.description: Step into Victorian London as consulting detectives unraveling supernatural mysteries that Holmes himself couldn't solve.
nominees.justification: M(2): Mostly reading, discussing clues, and logical deduction without complex systems. T(4): Investigating occult mysteries generates genuine detective atmosphere through narrative immersion. G(3): Meaningful choices about which leads to follow and theories to pursue. F(2): Fan expansion requires base game, some setup complexity with case materials. Ar(3): Atmospheric Victorian mystery art but fan production values limit polish.

nominees.name: Skull and Roses
nominees.description: Place your disc face-down and bluff whether it's a flower or skull, then bid on how many flowers you can reveal without hitting death.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple hidden information with bidding but minimal mechanical depth. T(2): Pirate/skull theme is decorative window dressing on pure bluffing. G(3): Meaningful bluffing and bidding decisions with psychological reads. F(1): Drop coasters on table and play immediately. Ar(3): Clean tribal designs but lacks atmospheric immersion.

nominees.name: 7 Wonders
nominees.description: Build one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World through three ages of simultaneous card drafting and civilization development.
nominees.justification: M(3): Card drafting with resource chains and wonder building. T(2): Ancient civilizations theme is pleasant but doesn't generate experience. G(3): Draft choices matter but limited interaction reduces impact. F(2): Multiple card decks and resource tracking add setup overhead. Ar(4): Antoine Bauza's elegant wonder boards and clean iconography.

nominees.name: Cache Moutons (reissued by Libellund in 2013 as Vite ! Cachons-nous !)
Small World
nominees.description: Draft fantasy races and special powers to conquer a shrinking world where civilizations rise, decline, and fall into legend.
nominees.justification: M(3): Race-power combos with area control and declining civilizations mechanics. T(2): Fantasy races feel generic, mechanics don't generate thematic experience. G(3): Meaningful combo selection and timing of going into decline. F(2): Multiple tokens per race create setup and management overhead. Ar(4): Miguel Coimbra's colorful fantasy art is charming and polished.

nominees.name: Dixit
nominees.description: Tell stories through surreal art cards where imagination becomes currency and creativity wins the day.
nominees.justification: M(1): Pick a card, tell a story — minimal mechanical complexity. T(2): Art creates mood but storytelling mechanics don't generate coherent themes. G(2): Creative expression matters but outcomes depend on group dynamics. F(1): Deal cards and start playing immediately. Ar(4): Marie Cardouat's dreamlike illustrations are genuinely evocative and beautiful.

nominees.name: Château Roquefort
nominees.description: Guide mice through a shifting cheese castle while avoiding the prowling cat in this dexterity-driven maze adventure.
nominees.justification: M(2): Roll-and-move with basic tile manipulation and memory elements. T(3): Cat-and-mouse chase feels authentic through movement restrictions and hiding. G(2): Dice-driven movement limits meaningful decision space significantly. F(2): Setup and component management moderate but rules accessible. Ar(3): Charming cartoon mice and castle art, functional but not striking.

nominees.name: Agricola
nominees.description: Build your medieval farm from nothing, feeding your family while expanding fields and livestock through fourteen grueling harvests.
nominees.justification: M(4): Deep worker placement with resource conversion, feeding pressure, and card synergies. T(2): Medieval farming theme is pleasant but mechanics don't generate farm life. G(4): Every worker placement matters with cascading consequences across seasons. F(3): Heavy setup, complex scoring, and dense rule interactions create overhead. Ar(3): Functional medieval art by Klemens Franz serves the game adequately.

nominees.name: Marrakech
nominees.description: Navigate a carpet merchant through Marrakech's marketplace, laying rugs and collecting payments from rivals who step on your wares.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple movement and tile-laying with basic area majority scoring. T(2): Marketplace theme present but mechanics don't generate merchant experience. G(2): Movement choices matter but limited tactical depth overall. F(1): Quick setup, simple rules, flows smoothly. Ar(4): Colorful Moroccan marketplace aesthetic with appealing rug tiles.

nominees.name: Princes of Florence
nominees.description: Renaissance patrons auction for artists, scholars, and jesters to create the most prestigious cultural salon in Florence.
nominees.justification: M(4): Multi-phase auction system with profession cards, buildings, and freedom cards creating deep interactions. T(1): Renaissance patronage is pure decoration over abstract auction mechanics. G(4): Every auction bid and profession hire shapes your cultural engine meaningfully. F(2): Multiple auction phases and scoring tracks add setup complexity. Ar(3): Functional Renaissance art that serves the theme adequately.

nominees.name: Du Balai !
nominees.description: Race your witch through a magical forest pathway, casting spells and dodging obstacles to reach the finish first.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic roll-and-move with simple spell card effects. T(2): Witch theme is decorative overlay on standard racing. G(2): Dice-driven movement with limited spell choices each turn. F(2): Standard setup and rules complexity for family game. Ar(2): Early 2000s fantasy art style, functional but unremarkable.

nominees.name: La Nuit des magiciens
nominees.description: Young wizards sneak through a magical academy in darkness, using only memory and touch to avoid detection.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple hidden movement with memory challenge, minimal mechanical depth. T(3): Darkness and sneaking create some wizard academy atmosphere. G(2): Limited meaningful choices, mostly about movement timing and positioning. F(2): Setup requires room darkening, physical components can be fiddly. Ar(3): Functional magical theme presentation without distinctive visual style.

nominees.name: Time's Up!
nominees.description: Describe celebrities through charades, one-word clues, then pure description across three frantic rounds with the same deck.
nominees.justification: M(1): Minimal mechanics - just draw cards and give clues. T(1): Celebrity theme is purely decorative window dressing. G(2): Some choice in clue-giving strategy but limited agency. F(1): Grab cards, set timer, explain rules instantly. Ar(2): Basic celebrity photos on cards with functional design.

nominees.name: Splash attack
nominees.description: Flick water balloons at opponents in this splashy dexterity game where getting soaked means getting eliminated.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple flicking mechanics with basic movement and elimination. T(2): Water balloon theme present but mechanics don't generate splash experience. G(2): Aiming choices matter but limited strategic depth overall. F(2): Physical setup and cleanup with water components adds friction. Ar(2): Basic toy-like components without atmospheric or elegant design.

nominees.name: Les Aventuriers du Rail

winners.description: Draft transportation cards and race across a fantasy realm to visit elven cities before your rivals claim the best routes.
winners.justification: M(2): Basic route-building with transportation drafting, limited interaction. T(2): Fantasy setting decorates mechanics without generating elven adventure. G(2): Route optimization with some blocking but predictable outcomes. F(2): Multi-phase setup and card management create moderate overhead. Ar(2): Dated 90s fantasy art lacks atmospheric punch or elegance.

winners.name: Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective
winners.description: Step into Victorian London as consulting detectives unraveling supernatural mysteries that Holmes himself couldn't solve.
winners.justification: M(2): Mostly reading, discussing clues, and logical deduction without complex systems. T(4): Investigating occult mysteries generates genuine detective atmosphere through narrative immersion. G(3): Meaningful choices about which leads to follow and theories to pursue. F(2): Fan expansion requires base game, some setup complexity with case materials. Ar(3): Atmospheric Victorian mystery art but fan production values limit polish.

winners.name: Railway Rivals
winners.description: Draw railway lines across a crayon-marked map and race to connect cities before your competitors claim the most profitable routes.
winners.justification: M(2): Simple track building with basic route optimization. T(2): Railway theme is decorative over mechanics. G(3): Route choices matter for network efficiency and blocking. F(3): Crayons, measuring, map marking creates table mess. Ar(2): Basic 1970s production with functional crayon-drawn maps.

winners.name: Scotland Yard
winners.description: One player becomes the elusive Mr. X, moving invisibly through London while detective players hunt him using only scattered clues.
winners.justification: M(3): Hidden movement with deduction and transportation network creates cat-and-mouse tension. T(4): Being the hunted criminal or pursuing detective IS the mechanic. G(3): Movement choices and deduction matter but limited options each turn. F(3): Dated components, setup overhead, and rules teach can drag. Ar(2): 1980s board design feels antiquated with bland London map.

winners.name: Enchanted Forest
winners.description: Race through an enchanted forest, secretly peek under fairy tale trees, and remember where treasures hide to be first to the castle.
winners.justification: M(2): Roll-and-move with memory element but limited mechanical depth. T(2): Fairy tale theme present but mechanics don't generate magical experience. G(2): Memory decisions matter but movement is mostly random. F(1): Simple family game with minimal setup requirements. Ar(3): Classic fairy tale illustration style, charming but not exceptional.

winners.name: Focus
winners.description: Stack checkers into towers and capture your opponent's pieces by moving the exact number of pieces in each stack.
winners.justification: M(2): Simple stacking and movement rules with modest tactical depth. T(1): Abstract game with no thematic coating or experience generation. G(3): Meaningful decisions about stack movement and capture timing. F(1): Classic abstract setup in seconds, teach immediately. Ar(2): Basic wooden pieces on plain board, purely functional.

winners.name: Rummikub
winners.description: Arrange numbered tiles into runs and groups, racing to empty your rack before opponents in this timeless pattern-matching contest.
winners.justification: M(2): Basic set collection with runs and groups, minimal interaction. T(1): No meaningful theme — abstract number manipulation. G(2): Tactical tile placement but heavily luck-dependent draws. F(1): Simple setup, teach in minutes. Ar(2): Functional numbered tiles with no visual appeal.

winners.name: Hare and Tortoise
winners.description: Race through the forest as either the steady tortoise or speedy hare in this classic fable reimagined as a strategic board game.
winners.justification: M(2): Simple race mechanics with basic action point allocation. T(2): Fable theme present but mechanics don't generate tortoise vs hare dynamics. G(2): Limited meaningful decisions in straightforward race format. F(2): Standard setup complexity for family racing game. Ar(3): Clean functional design appropriate for family audience.

nominees.name: Unlock! Game Adventures
nominees.description: Race against time to solve puzzles and escape digital adventures using only cards and a smartphone app.
nominees.justification: M(3): Card combinations with app integration create layered puzzle solving. T(3): Time pressure and clue discovery generate escape room tension reasonably well. G(3): Meaningful deduction choices but app guidance limits some agency. F(1): Just cards and phone app, instant setup and play. Ar(3): Clean card design but lacks atmospheric depth of premium games.

nominees.name: Unlock! Kids: Detektivgeschichten (Unlock! Kids: Detective Stories)
Pandemic Legacy: Season 2
nominees.description: The world has flooded and you must sail between floating havens, searching for supplies while the plague evolves and cities sink beneath the waves.
nominees.justification: M(4): Action points with legacy evolution, supply networks, and escalating threats. T(5): Every search, infection, and city loss IS the post-apocalyptic struggle. G(4): Meaningful choices about exploration, resource allocation, and permanent changes. F(2): Legacy stickers and evolving rules add setup complexity over time. Ar(4): Atmospheric post-flood world design with strong visual cohesion.

nominees.name: Die Tore der Welt (World Without End)
Gift Trap
nominees.description: Guess what gifts your friends would want while secretly choosing presents for them in this social deduction party game.
nominees.justification: M(1): Choose gifts from cards, reveal and guess - minimal mechanical interaction. T(1): Gift-giving theme is pure decoration over simple voting mechanics. G(2): Some meaningful choices in gift selection and guessing but highly subjective. F(1): Party game with immediate setup and simple rules explanation. Ar(1): Generic party game presentation with basic card layout and colors.

nominees.name: Space Alert
nominees.description: Your starship is under attack — you have 10 minutes of frantic real-time planning followed by watching your disaster unfold in slow motion.
nominees.justification: M(4): Complex real-time programming with movement tracks and threat resolution systems. T(5): Frantic countdown and communication chaos IS spaceship crisis management under fire. G(3): Meaningful planning decisions constrained by real-time pressure and limited information. F(3): CD soundtrack timing, complex setup, and overwhelming first-play experience. Ar(3): Functional sci-fi design that serves the mechanics without visual flair.

nominees.name: Agricola
nominees.description: Build your medieval farm from nothing, feeding your family while expanding fields and livestock through fourteen grueling harvests.
nominees.justification: M(4): Deep worker placement with resource conversion, feeding pressure, and card synergies. T(2): Medieval farming theme is pleasant but mechanics don't generate farm life. G(4): Every worker placement matters with cascading consequences across seasons. F(3): Heavy setup, complex scoring, and dense rule interactions create overhead. Ar(3): Functional medieval art by Klemens Franz serves the game adequately.

nominees.name: Caylus
nominees.description: Build a medieval castle town by placing workers along a road where the king's favor determines which buildings activate.
nominees.justification: M(4): Deep worker placement with building construction, road positioning, and royal favor mechanics. T(2): Medieval building theme overlays mechanics without generating the experience. G(4): Every worker placement cascades through road position and royal favor timing. F(3): Euro complexity with moderate setup and fiddly royal favor track. Ar(3): Functional medieval art that serves gameplay without atmospheric appeal.

nominees.name: Troia
nominees.description: Ancient warriors siege the legendary city of Troy through tactical movement and resource management in this early 2000s Euro design.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic action points and area control without deep synergies. T(2): Trojan War theme overlays standard mechanics without generating epic conflict. G(2): Tactical decisions present but limited by simple system. F(2): Typical Euro setup and rules overhead for the era. Ar(2): Functional early 2000s production values without atmospheric design.

nominees.name: Der Herr der Ringe (Lord of the Rings)
Arbos
nominees.description: Plant trees and cultivate forests in an abstract tile-laying game where nature grows through strategic placement.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic tile placement with simple adjacency rules and limited depth. T(2): Forest theme is decorative overlay on abstract mechanics. G(2): Placement choices matter but options are straightforward and predictable. F(3): Older game with dated components and potentially fiddly scoring. Ar(2): 1999 production values with functional but uninspiring forest artwork.

nominees.name: Kayanak
nominees.description: Inuit fishermen use magnetic rods to catch fish through holes they punch in a layered ice board.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple action point movement with magnetic fishing mechanics. T(2): Arctic fishing theme present but mechanics feel toy-like. G(2): Limited meaningful decisions beyond hole placement and movement. F(1): Quick setup with sturdy physical components. Ar(3): Functional arctic aesthetic but lacks atmospheric depth.

nominees.name: Zicke Zacke Hühnerkacke (Chicken Cha Cha Cha)
Die Magier
nominees.description: Medieval wizards compete in arcane duels using dice and cards to cast spells and claim magical supremacy.
nominees.justification: M(2): Simple dice rolling with basic card play mechanics. T(2): Wizard theme referenced but not deeply generated by mechanics. G(2): Limited meaningful choices constrained by dice luck. F(3): 1980s game with fiddly components and unclear rules overhead. Ar(2): Dated 1985 artwork lacks modern atmospheric appeal.

winners.name: Uisge
winners.description: Navigate the Scottish whisky trade as a merchant seeking profit in the Highland markets of 1983.
winners.justification: M(2): Basic trading mechanics with limited interconnection or depth. T(2): Whisky theme decorates rather than drives the trading experience. G(2): Standard merchant choices without cascading consequences or tension. F(2): 1980s production values suggest fiddly components and unclear rules. Ar(2): Dated aesthetic unlikely to create atmospheric immersion or visual appeal.

nominees.name: Wir füttern die kleinen Nilpferde
nominees.description: Feed colorful plastic balls to hungry hippos in this frantic marble-chomping race for children.
nominees.justification: M(1): Roll dice, move piece, no depth or systems. T(1): Hippo feeding is cosmetic label on abstract movement. G(1): Pure luck-based movement with no meaningful decisions. F(2): Simple setup but potential for scattered marbles and chaos. Ar(2): Bright plastic toy aesthetic lacks elegance or atmosphere.

nominees.name: Skript
nominees.description: An obscure 1982 card game lost to time with incomplete rules and no meaningful thematic identity.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic card play without complex interactions or systems. T(1): No discernible theme or fictional experience generated. G(2): Limited decision space in simple card mechanisms. F(5): 1982 game with incomplete/unclear rules creates massive play barriers. Ar(2): Dated 1982 production values with minimal visual appeal.

nominees.name: Ra: Strategy Among Hexagons
nominees.description: Ancient Egyptian god Ra oversees territorial control across a hexagonal board in this early abstract strategy game.
nominees.justification: M(1): Basic hex territory control with minimal mechanical depth. T(1): Ra theme is purely decorative over abstract mechanics. G(1): Limited decision tree in simple territorial gameplay. F(2): 1981 production values likely create setup friction. Ar(1): Early 80s abstract design lacks visual appeal.

nominees.name: Spiel
nominees.description: A mysterious German design experiment from 1994 that exists more as concept than playable game.
nominees.justification: M(1): Minimal or nonexistent mechanical systems based on available information. T(1): No coherent theme emerges from whatever mechanics exist. G(1): Unclear what meaningful decisions if any are available. F(5): Obscure rules, likely impossible to acquire or learn properly. Ar(1): No available art or production information suggests minimal presentation.

nominees.name: Rubik's Cube
nominees.description: Draw cards from a deck and manipulate them to recreate the patterns of a solved Rubik's Cube through card combinations.
nominees.justification: M(2): Card draw with pattern matching but minimal interlocking systems. T(1): Cube theme is cosmetic overlay on basic card mechanics. G(2): Some meaningful choices in card selection and combination timing. F(1): Simple card game with immediate setup and play. Ar(2): Basic 1980s card design with functional Rubik's Cube imagery.

nominees.name: Seti
nominees.description: Search for extraterrestrial intelligence by analyzing radio signals and making deductions about alien civilizations in this 1979 abstract deduction game.
nominees.justification: M(2): Basic deduction mechanics with limited interaction systems. T(2): SETI theme applied to abstract mechanics without generating experience. G(2): Some meaningful choices in signal analysis but constrained options. F(3): 1970s production values with fiddly components and dated rulebook. Ar(2): Functional but uninspiring 1979 graphic design and components.
